meaning: Charm or skill at flirting; short for charisma.
example: He talked to her for two minutes and got her number. Unreal rizz.
context: Praising (or roasting) someone's flirting game. 'W rizz' = good, 'no rizz' = none.

meaning: Delusional, usually about a crush or an unrealistic hope.
example: She thinks the celebrity replied to her story because he likes her. Delulu.
context: Teasing unrealistic expectations. 'Delulu is the solulu' jokingly means being delusional is the solution.

meaning: Your perceived coolness or presence; 'aura points' go up or down with your actions.
example: Tripping on stage in front of everyone: minus 1000 aura.
context: Scoring how cool or embarrassing something someone did was.

meaning: Average, mediocre, overhyped.
example: Everyone hyped that cafe, but honestly the food was mid.
context: Dismissive review of food, movies, songs or people's takes.

meaning: Doomed, in serious trouble, or completely exhausted.
example: Exam is tomorrow and I haven't opened the book. I'm cooked.
context: Self-roast when things are hopeless. 'We're so cooked' = we're done for.

term: Ate / Ate and left no crumbs
meaning: Did something perfectly or looked amazing.
example: Her presentation ate and left no crumbs.
context: Hyping a great performance, outfit or comeback.

meaning: Over-praising someone excessively, like a fanboy.
example: Bro, stop glazing Elon in every conversation.
context: Calling out someone who hypes a person way too much.

meaning: Exclamation (from 'goddamn') when reacting to someone's attractive body, usually their backside.
example: Used as a crude reaction comment under gym or dance videos.
context: Sexual reaction slang. Know it so you get the meme, but it's disrespectful to say about real people.

meaning: Someone who acts robotically, follows the crowd and has no original thoughts, like a background video-game character.
example: He just repeats whatever's trending. Total NPC behaviour.
context: Insulting someone as unoriginal or mindless.

meaning: A romantic/sexual relationship without labels or commitment.
example: We've been talking for 6 months but it's just a situationship.
context: Describing a confusing 'more than friends, less than partners' thing.

meaning: The mental fog from consuming too much low-quality online content; also the content itself.
example: Three hours of Skibidi edits. Pure brain rot.
context: Self-aware joke about doomscrolling. Oxford's Word of the Year 2024.

meaning: The number of people someone has had sex with.
example: Podcasts love asking guests about their body count.
context: Common in dating-podcast debates; often used judgmentally.

meaning: Someone who does way too much for a person they're attracted to, often without getting anything back.
example: He drove 40 km at midnight to deliver her momos. Simp.
context: Roasting over-eager romantic effort.

meaning: A sudden feeling of disgust that kills your attraction to someone.
example: He chewed with his mouth open and I instantly got the ick.
context: Dating talk: small things that turn you off.

meaning: 'For real' / 'no lie': I'm being serious.
example: This biryani is the best in Delhi, no cap.
context: Adds sincerity. 'Cap' = lie; 'that's cap' = that's false.

meaning: Lowkey = secretly or a little; highkey = openly, very much.
example: I lowkey want to skip the party. Highkey obsessed with this song.
context: Softening or amplifying a feeling.

meaning: A photo/video posted deliberately to attract sexual attention or compliments.
example: Shirtless gym mirror selfie at 1 AM? Thirst trap.
context: Calling out attention-seeking posts.

meaning: Manipulating someone into doubting their own memory or perception.
example: 'That never happened, you're imagining things,' when it clearly did.
context: Describing manipulative partners, bosses or family. Often overused for normal disagreements.

meaning: Overwhelming someone with affection and gifts early on to gain control.
example: Week one: flowers daily, 'you're my soulmate'. Week six: controlling who she meets.
context: Red flag in dating stories; often precedes manipulation.

meaning: Giving someone just enough attention (likes, occasional texts) to keep them hooked without commitment.
example: He never makes plans, just reacts to her stories every few days.
context: Dating behaviour that keeps someone waiting.

meaning: Ending contact suddenly with no explanation.
example: Three great dates, then she ghosted me.
context: Dating and even job hiring ('the recruiter ghosted me').

meaning: Having multiple romantic relationships at the same time with the knowledge and consent of everyone involved.
example: They're polyamorous: both have other partners and everyone knows.
context: Different from cheating: the key is consent and honesty. Often debated on podcasts.

meaning: A committed couple who agree that one or both can have sexual partners outside the relationship.
example: They opened the relationship after five years together.
context: Usually sexual non-exclusivity; polyamory usually also allows romantic bonds.

meaning: A strong emotional attachment to someone who causes you harm, created by cycles of abuse and affection.
example: She keeps going back to him even after the fights. It's a trauma bond.
context: Explains why people stay in toxic relationships.

meaning: Patterns of how people bond in relationships: secure, anxious, avoidant, or disorganised.
example: Anxious + avoidant: one chases, the other runs. Classic.
context: Pop-psych favourite for explaining dating dynamics.

meaning: Warning sign / positive sign about someone's behaviour.
example: Rude to waiters: red flag. Remembers your exam date: green flag.
context: Quick judgement of partners, friends, bosses.

meaning: Someone with excessive self-importance, need for admiration and lack of empathy. NPD is the clinical disorder.
example: Every conversation becomes about him. Narcissist energy.
context: Heavily overused online; a real diagnosis is rare and clinical.

meaning: Attributing your own unwanted feelings or behaviours to someone else.
example: He accuses her of cheating constantly. Turns out he was the one cheating.
context: 'That's projection' = you're describing yourself.

meaning: Acting as if you're the protagonist of life and everyone else is a side character.
example: Filming herself crying in public for content: main character syndrome.
context: Calling out self-centred or performative behaviour.

meaning: Limits you set on what behaviour you accept from others.
example: I don't answer work calls after 9 PM. That's a boundary.
context: Therapy-speak now common in everyday talk.

meaning: Historically a man whose wife cheats on him; now also a fetish where someone is aroused by their partner being with someone else.
example: Appears in cheating stories and as an insult ('cuck') online.
context: 'Cuck' is a common online insult for a weak or submissive man.

meaning: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: a hormonal condition causing irregular periods, acne, weight gain, excess hair growth and sometimes fertility issues.
example: She was diagnosed with PCOS and manages it with diet and exercise.
context: Very common (roughly 1 in 5 Indian women). Never joke about someone's weight because of it.

meaning: Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder: a mental health condition after a traumatic event, with flashbacks, anxiety and avoidance.
example: He has PTSD after the accident and avoids driving.
context: Often used jokingly ('that exam gave me PTSD'), but the real condition is serious.

meaning: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder: affects attention, impulse control and activity levels.
example: With ADHD, starting boring tasks feels physically hard.
context: Widely discussed online; self-diagnosis via reels is common and not reliable.

meaning: Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder: intrusive thoughts plus repetitive behaviours to relieve anxiety.
example: Real OCD isn't about liking neat desks. It's distressing.
context: 'I'm so OCD' for being tidy is a common misuse.

meaning: Sexually transmitted disease / infection, e.g. chlamydia, herpes, HIV.
example: Getting tested for STIs is normal and responsible.
context: Comes up in dating and health discussions.

meaning: If you know, you know: an inside reference only some people get.
example: That one canteen samosa... IYKYK.
context: Captions that hint at shared experiences.

meaning: Not gonna lie / to be honest.
example: NGL, the sequel was better.
context: Softens an honest opinion.

meaning: Point of view: on reels, it sets up a scenario you're meant to imagine being in.
example: POV: you open Insta for 5 minutes and it's 2 AM.
context: Reel/meme format.

meaning: Fear of missing out / joy of missing out.
example: Skipped the party and slept early. JOMO.
context: Social pressure vs. happily staying in.

meaning: Dual Income, No Kids: a couple who both earn and choose not to have children.
example: DINK couples are trending on finance reels.
context: Lifestyle and money debates.

meaning: Greatest Of All Time.
example: Kohli chasing is GOAT behaviour.
context: Sports and pop-culture hype.

meaning: In case you missed it.
example: ICYMI, the results are out.
context: Resharing news or posts.

meaning: Friends with benefits: friends who have sex without being in a relationship.
example: They said it was just FWB, but feelings happened.
context: Dating-podcast staple.

meaning: Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender, Queer/Questioning, Intersex, Asexual, and others.
example: The college started an LGBTQIA+ support group.
context: Umbrella term for gender and sexual minorities.

meaning: Systematic Investment Plan (investing a fixed amount monthly) / Exchange-Traded Fund (a fund traded like a stock).
example: Start a ₹1000 SIP in a Nifty 50 ETF or index fund.
context: Every finance influencer says these. Know them.

meaning: If you replace every part of a ship one by one, is it still the same ship?
example: 'After 10 years and a new everything, is it still the same band?' Ship of Theseus.
context: Used for identity questions: people changing, bands with new members, your body's cells.

meaning: From the cat that's 'both alive and dead' until observed; anything in two states until checked.
example: Schrödinger's exam result: I've both passed and failed until I open the portal.
context: Joke format for uncertain outcomes.

meaning: Two people each do better by betraying the other, but both end up worse than if they'd cooperated.
example: Both shops slash prices and both lose money. Prisoner's dilemma.
context: Explains trust, competition, cheating in relationships, arms races.

meaning: Continuing something only because you've already invested in it, even when quitting is smarter.
example: 'We've dated 4 years, I can't leave now.' That's the sunk cost fallacy.
context: Relationships, bad movies, failing projects.

meaning: People with little knowledge often overestimate their competence; experts often underestimate theirs.
example: Watched one reel on stocks, now he's giving tips. Dunning-Kruger.
context: Roasting overconfident beginners.

meaning: Trying to hide or censor something makes it spread even more.
example: The company deleted the tweet and now everyone's screenshotting it.
context: Named after Barbra Streisand suing to remove a photo of her house, which made it famous.

meaning: Too many options make us more anxious and less satisfied with our decision.
example: 40 minutes choosing on Netflix, then watching nothing.
context: Dating apps, shopping, careers.

meaning: Would you pull a lever to divert a trolley so it kills one person instead of five?
example: Self-driving cars face a real-life trolley problem.
context: Ethics debates; also a huge meme format with absurd versions.

meaning: We quickly return to a baseline happiness after good or bad events, so we keep wanting more.
example: New phone joy lasted a week. Hedonic treadmill.
context: Why money and upgrades don't keep us happy.

meaning: Buying one new thing triggers a spiral of buying more to match it.
example: Bought a new desk, now I 'need' a lamp, chair and monitor.
context: Consumerism and lifestyle creep.

meaning: The simplest explanation is usually the right one.
example: Wi-Fi's down. Occam's razor: the router's off, not a hacker.
context: Cutting through conspiracy theories.

meaning: When a measure becomes a target, it stops being a good measure.
example: Rank on 'lines of code' and developers write bloated code.
context: Exams, KPIs, follower counts.

meaning: People are less likely to help someone when others are present.
example: Everyone filmed the accident; nobody called an ambulance.
context: Social psychology and viral-video debates.

meaning: Roughly 80% of results come from 20% of causes.
example: 20% of chapters give 80% of exam marks. Study those first.
context: Productivity and business talk.

meaning: The universe is huge and old, so where is everybody? Why haven't we found aliens?
example: If aliens exist, why no contact? Fermi paradox.
context: Late-night podcast favourite.

meaning: Tiny changes can lead to huge, unpredictable consequences.
example: Missing one bus led me to meet my co-founder. Butterfly effect.
context: Life-story reflections.

meaning: Feeling like a fraud who'll be 'found out', despite real achievements.
example: Got into the internship but feel like they picked me by mistake.
context: Very common among students and new hires.

meaning: A dog sipping coffee in a burning room, pretending everything is OK.
example: Three deadlines tomorrow and I'm watching anime. This is fine.
context: Calm denial during chaos.

meaning: A self-styled 'lone wolf' who's successful outside social hierarchies. Mostly used ironically now.
example: Wakes at 4 AM, no friends, ice baths: 'sigma grindset'.
context: Mocking hustle-bro internet culture.

meaning: From 'Skibidi Toilet', a surreal YouTube series; now a nonsense word for anything weird or bad.
example: That outfit is so skibidi.
context: Peak Gen Alpha brain rot vocabulary.

meaning: Meme shorthand for anything bizarre or cursed ('only in Ohio').
example: Guy riding a buffalo on the highway? Bro's in Ohio.
context: Absurdist meme, not about the real state.

meaning: Go outside; you're too online.
example: Arguing with strangers in comments for 3 hours? Touch grass.
context: Telling someone to log off and get real.

meaning: Ironically relating to a (usually unhinged or tragic) fictional character.
example: Joker walking down stairs: 'he's just like me fr'.
context: Self-deprecating identification with a character.

meaning: When something occupies your thoughts constantly without you wanting it to.
example: That cringe thing I said in 2019 lives in my head rent free.
context: Can't stop thinking about something.

meaning: Mewing: tongue-posture trick for a sharper jaw. Looksmaxxing: obsessively optimising your looks.
example: Can't talk right now, I'm mewing (finger over lips).
context: Teen looks culture; the 'shh I'm mewing' gesture is a meme.

meaning: Ironic 'life motto' mocking toxic-but-confident behaviour.
example: Didn't share the notes and blamed you for asking. Gaslight, gatekeep, girlboss.
context: Satirising girlboss culture.

meaning: Something you think about weirdly often, from the trend about men thinking about the Roman Empire daily.
example: That 2012 cricket final is my Roman Empire.
context: 'What's your Roman Empire?' = what do you obsess over?

meaning: When a reply gets more likes than the original post, meaning people agree with the reply.
example: His hot take got ratioed into oblivion.
context: Twitter/X dunking culture.

meaning: An idealised, confident, attractive alpha man; 'Virgin vs Chad' memes compare insecure vs. confident behaviour.
example: Virgin 'reads the reviews' vs Chad 'orders the weirdest dish'.
context: Comparing behaviours humorously.

meaning: Reaction expressing disgust at something cringe or gross.
example: Pineapple on biryani? Brother ewwww.
context: Comment-section reaction.

meaning: It has the vibe of ___.
example: That office playlist? It's giving 2008 Bollywood.
context: Describing a vibe; 'it's giving' alone means it looks good.

meaning: Did exactly what the situation needed, perfectly.
example: Wore all black to the gothic party. Understood the assignment.
context: Compliment for nailing an event or task.

meaning: Format: reveal something indirectly through a detail.
example: Tell me you're an engineer without telling me: 'Maggi at 3 AM before the viva.'
context: Reel/caption format.
